To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exposure of the human prostate tumor subclone 1-LN (1-LN, 1-LN/PC-3, or PC-3-1L) to EMS or 5-azacitidine can alter the metastatic phenotype, and this change is reversible by exposure to 5-azaciidine.
exposure of 1-Ln human prostate tumor cells to the alkylating agent EMS resulted in heritable changes in their metastatic capacity in nude mice.
the metastatic behavior of a human prostate tumor cell subline in nude mice is altered after treatment with EMS, and the alteration can be reversed by 5-acytidine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metastatic potential of human prostate cancer cells and the factors that may influence this potential.
understanding how human tumor cell populations change during the process of evolution.
the development of new and effective methods of treating prostate cancer and with the mechanisms underlying the development of resistance to treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

“the metastatic phenotype of the human prostate tumor cells 1-LN is altered heritably by in vitro exposure of these cells to EMS and this altered phenotype can be reversed by exposure of the altered cells to 5-azacitidine”.
the metastatic potential of human tumor cells can be modified by treatment with EMS and 5-Aza.
the metastatic potential of human prostate tumor cell lines can be altered by treatment with EMS or 5-azacitidine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metastatic capacity of human tumor cells can be altered by in vitro treatment with EMS and that these changes can be reversed by exposure to 5-azacrytidine.

the metastatic potential of a human prostate tumor cell line in athymic mice can be altered by in vitro chemical treatment and that the altered metastatic phenotype can be reversed by exposure to the drug 5-azacrytidine.
the metastatic potential of human prostate cancer can be heritably changed by in vitro treatment with chemical mutagens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metastatic potential of prostate cancer cells is heritable.
the metastatic capacity of human prostate tumor sublines in nude mice can be reproducibly altered by in vitro chemical mutagenesis and “reverted” by exposure to 5-azacitidine.
it is possible to alter the metastatic phenotype in human prostate cancer cells in athymc mice by exposure to EMS and “reversion by exposure to 5-azacitidine.
